Credential body: Provincial and territorial translator associations, federated through CTTIC (Quebec is separate)
Credentials: Provincial certified translator, terminologist, or interpreter titles
Official search or register: Provincial association in the applicant's province of residence
Notes: CTTIC does not grant certification itself. The power to certify is provincial.

Used for government work: Varies. No national translator certification; court interpreting is handled by state and federal programs (not researched)
Official search or register: ATA Language Services Directory (free to use; filter for certified translators)
Notes: ATA is not a government body. Directory terms of use not confirmed.

Credential body: CATTI management (National Accreditation Test for Translators and Interpreters)
Credentials: CATTI Level I, II, III for translation and interpreting
Official search or register: Not verified. Official lookup portal not confirmed
Notes: National test exists. Official lookup portal and government requirements not verified.

Credentials: Recognised Practising Interpreter (RPI), Certified Practising Interpreter (CPI), Certified Interpreter (CI), and NAATI certified translation
Used for government work: Yes: NAATI certification is the credential Australian government agencies use
Notes: Directory describes itself as the official register. Terms of use not confirmed. Automated queries are disallowed by robots.txt.

Model: Government requirement for NAATI; professional association for members
Credentials: NAATI RPI, CPI or CI for government interpreting
Used for government work: Yes: since 1 July 2024, interpreters working for government agencies must hold NAATI certification
Official search or register: Not confirmed. NZSTI's directory location was not confirmed
Notes: Use NAATI credentials for government work. NZSTI membership is separate.

Credentials: SATI accreditation; sworn translator status (exam recognised by the High Court)
Used for government work: Varies. SATI accreditation has no official recognition in South African law
Notes: Sources are mixed in age. Confirm the current register before relying on it.

Credentials: Öffentlich bestellt und allgemein beeidigt (publicly appointed and sworn) translator or interpreter
Used for government work: Yes for court and authority work: the oath applies before all federal and state courts
Official search or register: Federal database: justiz-dolmetscher.de; BDÜ directory: bdue.de
Notes: No single nationwide court register found. Lists are not complete, so check the relevant state.

Credential body: Institute of Translation and Interpreting (ITI); Chartered Institute of Linguists (CIOL)
Used for government work: Varies. Certified translations can be self-certified by an ITI Fellow or Member
Official search or register: ITI online directory: https://iti.org.uk/language-services; CIOL Find a Translator
Notes: Translation is not legally regulated in the UK, so the directory is how you confirm membership.

Credential body: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation (Oficina de Interpretación de Lenguas)
Used for government work: Yes: sworn translations are accepted by courts and administrative bodies
Notes: Governed by Royal Decree 724/2020. Catalan, Galician, and Basque exams are run by regional governments.
